slides.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
slides.tldr: LLMs fail to replicate collective social effects
slides.highlight: This paper identifies a 'bias cascade' where LLMs align with social knowledge but fail to reproduce collective outcomes in simulations, a critical limitation for MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLMs align with social knowledge but fail to replicate collective effects due to bias cascades in simulation.
card.key_idea: Introduces REFLEX benchmark to compare knowledge judgment with effect simulation, demonstrating that micro-level alignment does not guarantee macro-level causal fidelity.
card.evaluation: Assessed 8 LLMs on 30 counterfactual tasks using Net Directional Score; simulation scores (~0.45) significantly lag behind knowledge scores (~0.85).
card.limitation: Current models remain inadequate for reliable social simulation, as errors cascade through dynamic interactions despite accurate individual judgments.

slides.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
slides.highlight: This work presents DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM that unifies speaker diarization, utterance timing, and visual description into a single model, achieving high accuracy in identifying who speaks when and how they appear. This aligns with HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception by integrating precise temporal and identity cues for hybrid human-AI team state analysis.

card.one_liner: DiaCap jointly learns utterance timing and audiovisual diarization via SFT and RL for precise dialogue captioning.
card.key_idea: Unifies timing and diarization in one model, trained on 225K synthetic clips and refined via RL with fine-grained feedback on 2.9K human-corrected clips.
card.evaluation: Tested on extended DiaDemBench; outperforms Gemini 4 Argon in timestamp accuracy (76.59 vs 42.76) while matching diarization performance.
card.limitation: Struggles with small/distant faces lacking lip-motion evidence and relies on off-the-shelf transcripts, where errors degrade diarization.

slides.title: BEARING: Who Is Talking to Whom? Grounding Acoustic Direction in Vision for Online Multi-Party Conversation
slides.highlight: BEARING introduces an online, geometry-first approach that fuses microphone array direction with visual cues to resolve speaker and addressee identities in multi-party conversations, directly supporting HyECHO's goals of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception and diarization.

card.one_liner: BEARING grounds acoustic direction in vision to improve online multi-party speaker identification and alignment.
card.key_idea: Registers microphone array direction into camera images as visual prompts and verifiable rewards for online speaker/addressee detection.
card.evaluation: Tested on AMI, EasyCom, AVDIAR; direction prompts raise speaker accuracy 20.6%, verifiable rewards outperform self-evaluation baselines.
card.limitation: Co-location study limited to AVDIAR; direction reward accuracy depends on array quality; online registration learning causes initial dips.

slides.title: EvoMisty: Building, Optimizing, and Evolving Capabilities on a Social Robot
slides.highlight: EvoMisty presents a plugin-based framework where coding agents build, verify, and optimize robot capabilities on a physical social robot, directly supporting RwB's goal of AI-mediated embodied learning and adaptive human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EvoMisty enables coding agents to autonomously build, optimize, and evolve robot capabilities from documentation.
card.key_idea: A four-stage framework where agents build verified atomic capabilities, solve tasks, optimize metrics via execution data, and distill reusable skills.
card.evaluation: Tested on Misty II with Claude Code and Codex; verified 109 capabilities, completed 35 tasks, and improved 7 metrics across 5 tasks.
card.limitation: Validated only on Misty II; relies on human feedback for verification and final performance depends on initial agent implementation.

slides.title: Unifying Partner and Environment Diversity to Improve Human-AI Coordination
slides.highlight: This work introduces Cross Environment Co-Play (CECP), a framework that jointly models partner and environment diversity to improve zero-shot coordination in novel settings, directly addressing ADAM-CHAT's goal of robust ad-hoc human-AI teaming in unseen environments.

card.one_liner: CECP unifies partner and environment diversity to improve zero-shot human-AI coordination.
card.key_idea: Two-stage training: self-play population across diverse environments, then cooperator training against this pool with next-state prediction.
card.evaluation: Tested on Overcooked and foraging tasks with held-out partners/environments; validated with 73 humans; outperformed baselines.
card.limitation: Performance depends on diversity in training populations; latents capture broad skill levels rather than fine-grained intent.

slides.title: Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that LLM personas apply systematic, value-congruent priors when evaluating political speakers, showing that source attribution significantly alters sentiment independent of content. This is relevant to HyECHO as it highlights the need for robust addressee and listener modeling to account for identity-driven biases in synthetic human-AI team interactions.

card.one_liner: LLM personas penalize political messages based on speaker identity, mirroring human ideological congruence and source cues.
card.key_idea: Fully crossed speaker-attribution experiment using value-grounded LLM personas to measure stance shifts when identical posts are attributed to different political leaders.
card.evaluation: 322,470 persona-post quartets across four topics; validated against 48 CIS barometers, showing ordinal alignment with human data up to the model's knowledge cutoff.
card.limitation: Alignment is ordinal not quantitative; personas reflect dated political associations (pre-2024 cutoff) and cannot substitute for real-time public opinion surveys.

slides.title: YYForce Launches Humanoid Concierge Robot for Hotel Deployment
slides.highlight: The deployment of a trained humanoid concierge robot in a hospitality setting offers practical insights into real-world human-robot interaction and service delivery, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Who Attributes a Mind to Whom? Mutual Theory of Mind in Simulated User-Assistant Conversation
slides.tldr: MUTUAL MIND ATTRIBUTION IN SIMULATED CHATS
slides.highlight: This study introduces a message-level framework to quantify mutual theory of mind in user-assistant interactions, revealing how user characteristics and AI behaviors influence mind attribution. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT for understanding the dynamics of intent inference and the risks of over-reliance in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Simulated user traits, not assistant style, primarily drive mind attribution in AI conversations.
card.key_idea: Simulated user-assistant chats measure four-directional mind attribution via LLM judges and encoders, varying user personas and assistant styles.
card.evaluation: 23,400 simulated conversations across 13 model combinations; validated against human coders (Krippendorff's alpha ~0.90) and fine-tuned ModernBERT.
card.limitation: Simulated users are not humans; results may overestimate user-side effects and underestimate assistant-side impacts compared to real interactions.

slides.title: YYForce Launches Six Seven Humanoid Concierge for Novotel Singapore
slides.highlight: The deployment of a humanoid concierge in a commercial hospitality setting provides a real-world case study for evaluating social robot interaction and user acceptance in service environments.

slides.title: Sarvam AI Releases Open-Weight 105B Checkpoint for Enterprise Agents
slides.highlight: Sarvam AI has released an open-weight 105B parameter model checkpoint specifically targeted at enterprise agent applications.

slides.title: EMIP: Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform
slides.highlight: EMIP provides a virtual environment for studying cooperation between humans and embodied AI agents, supporting full-duplex speech and simultaneous physical interaction. This aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction by offering a reusable platform for multi-party experimental setups.

card.one_liner: EMIP is a Minecraft-based platform enabling concurrent speech and physical interaction among multiple humans and AI agents.
card.key_idea: Integrates full-duplex speech, simultaneous physical actions, and Model Context Protocol interfaces for LLM-driven agent control in shared virtual environments.
card.evaluation: Demonstrated via usage examples of concurrent speech and task coordination; no quantitative benchmarks or baseline comparisons are reported.
card.limitation: Performance depends on LLM inference and human response times, limiting simulation speedup; utility across diverse tasks remains to be empirically evaluated.

slides.title: Universal AI Model for Neuroscience
slides.highlight: Scientists have developed a powerful AI model designed to serve as a universal language for neuroscience, potentially standardizing data interpretation across the field.

slides.title: Nio launches NWM 3.0 world model and Nomi Intelligence 4.0
slides.highlight: Nio has released NWM 3.0, a new world model, alongside Nomi Intelligence 4.0.

slides.title: VidForce: Predicting Force-Aware Articulation by Observing Humans
slides.highlight: VidForce estimates interaction trajectories and force profiles from third-person RGB video using learned physical prototypes, aligning with MOSAIC's goal of deriving physics-based skill metrics from visual observations.

card.one_liner: VidForce estimates interaction trajectories and force profiles from third-person video using learned physical prototypes.
card.key_idea: Uses learned force prototypes as priors, refined by a joint conditional flow that couples trajectory tracking with force estimation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Hoi! dataset; achieves 6.6cm ATE and 4.81N peak-force MAE, outperforming baselines in trajectory and force recovery.
card.limitation: Relies on paired instrumented gripper data for supervision, limiting applicability to domains without such specialized measurements.

slides.title: Escaping the Instruction Black Hole of Vision-Language-Action Policies via Optimal-Transport Wormholes
slides.tldr: OPTIMAL TRANSPORT FOR VLA TASK SWITCHING
slides.highlight: This work addresses the 'instruction black hole' in Vision-Language-Action policies by using Optimal Transport to seamlessly relocate robots to new task states, a mechanism directly relevant to MOSAIC's goal of aligning human-AI intent during dynamic coadaptation.

card.one_liner: Wormhole escapes VLA instruction black holes by relocating robots via optimal transport, achieving 93% success.
card.key_idea: Training-free plug-in uses optimal transport to move the robot into the new task's committed state, bypassing the policy's inability to process mid-execution instruction changes.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO with π0 and π0.5; raised committed-switch success from ~1% to 93%, outperforming scripted retreats with lower action discontinuity.
card.limitation: Requires access to successful execution states for the new task and relies on optimal transport coupling, which may be computationally intensive or sensitive to state distribution mismatches.

slides.title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations
slides.highlight: This paper introduces ClusterVAD, an unsupervised voice activity detection method using frozen speech foundation model representations, which aligns with HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception by enabling robust speech/non-speech segmentation without labeled data.

card.one_liner: Unsupervised VAD using frozen SSL representations and sonority-based clustering achieves competitive detection without labeled data.
card.key_idea: Clusters whitened SSL features from auxiliary speech, labels clusters via sonority, and applies a threshold-free HMM decision for robust detection.
card.evaluation: Tested on 12 benchmarks (AMI, AliMeeting, Torgo, etc.) using DetER and Event-F1; outperforms unsupervised baselines and matches supervised models.
card.limitation: High computational cost from SSL encoders; threshold-free mode is unreliable on short utterances; lacks speaker-aware pause merging.

slides.title: Knocking on Minds Door; A Mixed-Methods Field Study of a Voice LLM Companion in Older Adults Daily Lives
slides.tldr: VOICE LLM COMPANION FOR OLDER ADULTS
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates how voice-based LLM companions utilizing persona, memory, and conversation rules can reduce emotional loneliness in older adults, offering insights relevant to HyECHO's focus on social perception and engagement in human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: Voice LLM companions reduce loneliness in older adults by leveraging familiar phone-call metaphors and persistent memory.
card.key_idea: A proactive voice agent using a grandchild persona, phone-call interface, and temporal knowledge graph for personalized, memory-driven conversations.
card.evaluation: Two-week field study with 33 Korean older adults; significant decreases in loneliness and depression scores via pre/post surveys and call logs.
card.limitation: Small sample size, lack of control group, and turn-taking difficulties due to voice activity detection delays may limit generalizability.

slides.title: Ego2Real: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Visuo-Tactile Demonstrations
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that augmenting egocentric visual demonstrations with tactile sensing significantly improves the fidelity of hand-object interaction reconstruction and policy learning, directly addressing the need for physics-based and tacit skill estimation in MOSAIC's coadaptive loop.

card.one_liner: Ego2Real transfers bimanual dexterous skills from egocentric visuo-tactile human demos to robots.
card.key_idea: Combines tactile-guided hand-object reconstruction with contact-informed reinforcement learning to resolve visual ambiguities and guide policy training.
card.evaluation: Tested on Bottle Handover and Box Rotation tasks in simulation and real-world, comparing against REGRIND, SPIDER, and MANIPTRANS.
card.limitation: Requires specific tactile gloves, known object meshes, and simulation; currently limited to rigid-object tasks.

slides.title: Do Vision-Language Models Know Their Own Visual Weaknesses? Probing Capability-Level Metacognition
slides.tldr: VLMs LACK EXPLICIT METACOGNITION OF VISUAL WEAKNESSES
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that vision-language models largely fail to predict their own visual weaknesses in advance, though latent signals in answer probabilities reveal these limitations during task execution. This finding is critical for ADAM-CHAT, as it highlights the gap between implicit and explicit self-monitoring that AI teammates must bridge to achieve reliable meta-cognitive self-correction in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: VLMs lack metacognition about visual weaknesses, but answer probabilities reveal model-specific limitations.
card.key_idea: Evaluates VLM self-prediction of accuracy across tasks/degradations, separating shared difficulty from model-specific weaknesses using partial correlations.
card.evaluation: Tested 33 VLMs on 13 axes from 19 benchmarks; compared stated predictions, fine-tuned models, and answer probabilities against actual accuracy.
card.limitation: Stated predictions remain poor even after training; only internal answer probabilities reliably expose model-specific weaknesses.

slides.title: Honest but Wrong: Formalizing Retraction in the Ethics of Speech Acts
slides.highlight: This work formalizes the moral duty to retract erroneous assertions, offering a framework for evaluating speech act corrections that could inform HyECHO's modeling of group norms and engagement in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: Formalizes retraction duties for honest but false assertions using deontological and consequentialist logic.
card.key_idea: Extends belief-based speech act frameworks with FIPA-ACL disconfirm, adding persistent honesty maxims to mandate retracting erroneous truths.
card.evaluation: Implemented in Answer Set Programming; tested on legal-advice scenarios, showing deontologism always requires retraction while consequentialism depends on harm prevention.
card.limitation: Assumes later beliefs are given inputs rather than derived from observations, and lacks nested belief modeling for complex epistemic states.

slides.title: Read My Lips: Context-aware Lip Reading Using Language and Audio-Visual Models
slides.highlight: This paper presents a method for recovering speech by combining lip reading, language models, and audio-visual generation, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in noisy or partially observable environments.

card.one_liner: RML combines lip reading, language models, and audio-visual generation to restore speech from corrupted audio.
card.key_idea: Integrates visual articulation, linguistic context, and acoustic evidence via adaptive test-time selection to handle missing or noisy speech.
card.evaluation: Tested on TalkVid, VoxMM, and hard sets; outperforms baselines in WER and span recovery across noise, silence, and occlusion.
card.limitation: Performance relies on lip reader accuracy; errors persist when visual evidence is weak and context is ambiguous.

slides.title: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution
slides.highlight: CHASE demonstrates how curiosity-guided investigation and on-demand skill acquisition can resolve uncertainty in embodied tasks, offering a potential mechanism for the skill acquisition component of MOSAIC's coadaptive loop.

card.one_liner: CHASE enables robots to resolve uncertainty and acquire missing skills via curiosity-driven planning and verified execution.
card.key_idea: Couples hypothesis-driven investigation with on-demand skill acquisition, balancing information value, capability expansion, and execution costs.
card.evaluation: Tested in BEHAVIOR-1K simulation and real robots; achieves 50–80% success under combined gaps, outperforming fixed-skill baselines.
card.limitation: High acquisition cost (up to 40 mins) and reliance on accurate cost estimation and validated skill scopes for generalization.

slides.title: When Skills Fail to Compose: Compatibility and Retention in Language Models
slides.highlight: This study reveals that independently acquired skills often fail to compose effectively in language models, highlighting critical challenges in compatibility and retention for self-evolving agents.

card.one_liner: Individually proficient soft-prompt skills fail to compose in one call, requiring separate execution or careful repair.
card.key_idea: Evaluates composition of independently learned soft prompts on frozen LLMs, analyzing interference, retention, and transfer across digit and record-editing tasks.
card.evaluation: Tested on Qwen/Gemma models using synthetic digit transformations and record edits, measuring one-call vs. two-call accuracy and post-repair retention.
card.limitation: Limited to synthetic tasks and soft prompts; findings may not generalize to complex real-world agent skills or other parameter-efficient methods.

slides.title: Who Is Ego? Scaling Cross-View Camera Wearer Identification and Segmentation beyond Humans
slides.highlight: This work advances ego-exo view alignment by identifying camera wearers through geometric epipole constraints, directly supporting MOSAIC's goal of robust multi-view proficiency estimation across diverse agents.

card.one_liner: Geometric method identifies camera wearers across humans, robots, and animals using ego-exo image pairs.
card.key_idea: Leverages epipolar geometry via VGGT-Ω to rank candidates by angular offset and distance, enabling training-free identification and segmentation.
card.evaluation: Tested on FindEgo-1M (1.16M pairs) and TF2023; outperforms baselines and LLMs in accuracy and speed across diverse wearer types.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate 3D pose estimation from VGGT-Ω, which may degrade in extreme occlusions or ambiguous geometric configurations.

slides.title: Measuring Counterfactual Credit in a Replayable Wildfire-Suppression Benchmark
slides.highlight: This work introduces a replayable multi-agent benchmark for directly measuring counterfactual credit, revealing that critics trained on team returns often fail to accurately assign individual action credit. This is relevant to MIMIC as it provides a rigorous method for evaluating agent contribution in complex, stochastic cooperative simulations.

card.one_liner: Replayable wildfire benchmark shows learned critics misassign credit despite accurate return prediction.
card.key_idea: FLARE uses common random numbers to compute exact difference rewards for training and replay-based references to audit learned counterfactual credit.
card.evaluation: MAPPO on 8 seeds; simulator credit reduced burn score to 20.9% vs 26.6% shared reward; critics overestimated credit 9-42x.
card.limitation: Replay noise limits action ranking precision; findings specific to MAPPO and COMA-style critics in this stochastic environment.
